title: Sorting Among the First Programs Ever Written
explainer: Sorting wasn't a late addition to computing — it was one of the first real problems tackled on stored-program machines. A 1945 manuscript by John von Neumann, written for the EDVAC and only published in full decades later, contains a routine for merging two sorted sequences that historians consider among the earliest surviving examples of a modern computer program, and the direct ancestor of merge sort. That sorting was already a priority before general-purpose computers even existed says something about how fundamental the problem is.
